slides.title: The nurse on a medical-surgical unit has been made aware of the following client
text: Question: The nurse on a medical-surgical unit has been made aware of the following client situations. The nurse should first plan to assess the client who
A. has type 2 diabetes mellitus with a premeal glucose of 85 mg/dL and a postmeal glucose of 220 mg/dL.
B. is 24 hours postoperative from abdominal surgery and wound drainage has changed from sanguineous to serosanguineous over 2 hours.
C. is preparing for a colonoscopy and whose BP was 128/74 mm Hg and is now 106/60 mm Hg.
D. has acute pancreatitis and reports an unchanged pain level of 7/10, 30 minutes after an oral pain medication.
Correct answer: C. is preparing for a colonoscopy and whose BP was 128/74 mm Hg and is now 106/60 mm Hg.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:

Priority = unstable/changing physiology first. A falling BP during bowel prep suggests fluid volume deficit (hypovolemia) and is the only true change that threatens circulation. Sanguineous→serosanguineous drainage is the expected healing progression, and a postmeal glucose of 220 is an expected rise. Unchanged pain is a concern, but it is not as acutely unstable as dropping BP.

slides.title: The nurse has received hand-off report and is assigning tasks to unlicensed assi
text: Question: The nurse has received hand-off report and is assigning tasks to unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP). Which task should the nurse instruct the UAP to perform first?
A. Obtain a sputum specimen from a client with suspected pulmonary TB.
B. Obtain a capillary blood glucose on a client who had a hypoglycemic episode 30 minutes ago and received IV dextrose.
C. Turn and reposition a client who was last turned 2 hours ago.
D. Deliver a lunch tray to a client returning from radiology who has been NPO since breakfast.
Correct answer: C. Turn and reposition a client who was last turned 2 hours ago.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:

Delegation: UAP perform routine tasks on STABLE clients. A client who just had hypoglycemia and IV dextrose is unstable; the RN must monitor and interpret that glucose. Of the remaining tasks, turning is time-critical now (q2h to prevent pressure injury). The sputum specimen is routine, and the NPO client should be cleared by the RN before eating.

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comprehensive B" gives a different answer: "Obtain a capillary blood glucose on a client who had a hypoglycemia episode 30 minutes ago and received dextrose IV.". Yours here is "Turn and reposition a client who was last turned 2 hours ago.". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: The nurse on a pediatric unit is reviewing client data. Which client should the
text: Question: The nurse on a pediatric unit is reviewing client data. Which client should the nurse plan to see first?
A. The infant with pertussis receiving oxygen via nasal cannula.
B. The adolescent with sickle cell crisis who is being discharged.
C. The toddler with bilateral arm casts who needs breakfast fed to them.
D. The school-aged child with type 1 diabetes who requires blood glucose monitoring.
Correct answer: A. The infant with pertussis receiving oxygen via nasal cannula.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
ABCs: an infant with pertussis has a high risk of apnea and airway obstruction and is already requiring oxygen. The other three are stable, routine needs.

slides.title: A newly hired nurse is discussing fiscally responsible practice with the precept
text: Question: A newly hired nurse is discussing fiscally responsible practice with the preceptor. Which statement requires follow-up?
A. “Involving the family in client care activities is an example of fiscal responsibility.”
B. “Engaging in safe clinical practice to avoid personal injuries is an example of fiscal responsibility.”
C. “Completing assigned nursing care during scheduled hours is a way to demonstrate fiscal responsibility.”
D. “Following evidence-based best practice guidelines demonstrates fiscal responsibility.”
Correct answer: A. “Involving the family in client care activities is an example of fiscal responsibility.”
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:

Fiscal responsibility means using resources wisely: avoiding injury and errors, completing work within scheduled hours (no overtime), and following EBP to prevent costly complications. Involving family is family-centered care and does not directly relate to cost, so it is the statement that needs follow-up.

slides.title: The preceptor observes a newly hired nurse teaching a client with pelvic inflamm
text: Question: The preceptor observes a newly hired nurse teaching a client with pelvic inflammatory disease who does not speak English. Which action requires intervention?
A. Contacting the charge nurse to obtain a facility-approved interpreter.
B. Providing written instructions in the client’s primary language.
C. Using a facility-approved telephone interpretation service.
D. Having a family member who speaks both languages interpret the instructions.
Correct answer: D. Having a family member who speaks both languages interpret the instructions.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:

Use a qualified, facility-approved interpreter. Family members may alter or omit information, and the topic is sensitive (confidentiality/HIPAA). Written materials in the client’s language and phone interpretation are acceptable.

slides.title: A client in labor has just had spontaneous rupture of membranes. Which finding i
text: Question: A client in labor has just had spontaneous rupture of membranes. Which finding is a priority to report to the PHCP?
A. Contractions lasting 60 seconds.
B. New appearance of late decelerations.
C. Maternal temperature of 99.5° F.
D. Four contractions in a 10-minute period.
Correct answer: B. New appearance of late decelerations.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:

Late decelerations indicate uteroplacental insufficiency (fetal hypoxia). After rupture, cord prolapse/placental problems are also a concern. The other findings are normal for labor (contractions ≤5 in 10 min, 60 s duration, T <100.4° F).

slides.title: The preceptor observes a newly hired nurse caring for clients. Which action indi
text: Question: The preceptor observes a newly hired nurse caring for clients. Which action indicates correct care?
A. Placing an N95 on a client with active TB before transport to a long-term care facility.
B. Administering oral pain medication to a client 30 minutes before discharge.
C. Using a 23-gauge, 1-inch needle for an IM injection in the deltoid.
D. Teaching a client with a new ileostomy to empty the bag 30 minutes after eating.
Correct answer: C. Using a 23-gauge, 1-inch needle for an IM injection in the deltoid.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:

IM injection: 22–25 gauge, 1–1.5 in (adult deltoid) is appropriate. The CLIENT with TB wears a surgical mask (the nurse wears the N95). Ostomy pouches are emptied when 1/3 full and not right after meals, when output peaks.

slides.title: In an outpatient clinic, which client should the nurse have the PHCP see first?
text: Question: In an outpatient clinic, which client should the nurse have the PHCP see first?
A. 15-year-old with a bull’s-eye rash 2 days after a camping trip.
B. 37-year-old with polycystic kidney disease and lumbar pain when ambulating.
C. 45-year-old with pleurisy and worsening shortness of breath.
D. 57-year-old with Graves’ disease who has heat intolerance and diaphoresis.
Correct answer: C. 45-year-old with pleurisy and worsening shortness of breath.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
Worsening shortness of breath is an airway/breathing (ABC) problem. Heat intolerance in Graves’ disease, flank pain with PKD, and an early Lyme rash are expected or less urgent.

slides.title: The nurse is aware of the following client situations. The nurse should first pl
text: Question: The nurse is aware of the following client situations. The nurse should first plan to see the client who has
A. cervical cancer, receives internal radiation therapy, and whose partner has been at the bedside for 2 hours.
B. neutropenia (WBC 3,000/mm³) and is eating homemade cookies from a visitor.
C. bone marrow suppression, receiving epoetin alfa, with BP changing from 140/94 to 124/80.
D. thrombocytopenia and a family member has brought fresh fruit and flowers.
Correct answer: A. cervical cancer, receives internal radiation therapy, and whose partner has been at the bedside for 2 hours.
Topic: Oncology & Radiation
notes: Rationale:

Internal (sealed) radiation: visitors are limited (about 30 minutes/day) and must stay ~6 ft from the source. A partner at the bedside for 2 hours is being unsafely exposed, so the nurse intervenes. The other situations are not immediate hazards for those diagnoses.

slides.title: A male client has full-thickness burns to 50% of the lower body. It is a priorit
text: Question: A male client has full-thickness burns to 50% of the lower body. It is a priority to notify the PHCP if the client has a
A. hematocrit of 60%.
B. SpO₂ of 91%.
C. urinary output of 100 mL over the past 2 hours.
D. temperature of 104.2° F.
Correct answer: D. temperature of 104.2° F.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:

A temperature of 104.2° F suggests sepsis/infection, the leading cause of death in burn clients. Hemoconcentration (high Hct) is an expected early finding, and 50 mL/hr urine output is adequate (≥30 mL/hr).

slides.title: Following an explosion at a local factory, the ED nurse triages clients. Which c
text: Question: Following an explosion at a local factory, the ED nurse triages clients. Which client is the priority for treatment?
A. Closed tibia fracture with severe pain.
B. Type 1 diabetes who feels shaky with clammy skin.
C. Large head wound with exposed gray matter and RR of 6.
D. Second-degree burns to chest and arms with RR greater than 30.
Correct answer: D. Second-degree burns to chest and arms with RR greater than 30.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:

Triage: treat life-threatening but salvageable problems first. Burns of the chest with tachypnea suggest airway/inhalation injury. The head wound with exposed brain and RR 6 is likely expectant (unsurvivable).

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client with severe hypocalcemia. Which should be inclu
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client with severe hypocalcemia. Which should be included in the plan of care?
A. Encourage foods high in phosphorus.
B. Measure urine output every 2 hours.
C. Place the client on seizure precautions.
D. Encourage increased fluid intake.
Correct answer: C. Place the client on seizure precautions.
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Low calcium increases neuromuscular excitability: tetany, laryngospasm, seizures. Phosphorus is inversely related to calcium and would worsen the imbalance.

slides.title: Which action by the nurse is appropriate?
text: Question: Which action by the nurse is appropriate?
A. Placing a client who had a stem cell transplant in contact isolation.
B. Having a client with pertussis wear a surgical mask during transport.
C. Initiating airborne precautions for a client with epiglottitis.
D. Wearing an N95 when caring for a client with impetigo.
Correct answer: B. Having a client with pertussis wear a surgical mask during transport.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Pertussis = droplet precautions; the client wears a surgical mask when transported. A transplant recipient needs protective (reverse) isolation, epiglottitis is droplet, and impetigo is contact.

slides.title: In an ambulatory center, the nurse should immediately remove from the waiting ro
text: Question: In an ambulatory center, the nurse should immediately remove from the waiting room and place in an exam room the client who has
A. heart failure and a 3 lb weight gain in 3 days.
B. a fever of 101.8° F, headache, vomiting, and photophobia.
C. myasthenia gravis, left ptosis, and a nasal-sounding voice.
D. a 1 mm flat, red area at the site of a Mantoux test given 48 hours ago.
Correct answer: B. a fever of 101.8° F, headache, vomiting, and photophobia.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:

Fever, headache, vomiting and photophobia suggest meningitis (droplet precautions), so protect others and expedite care. A 1 mm area is a negative PPD; the HF and MG clients need follow-up but are not infectious.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client with a sealed radiation implant. Which precauti
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client with a sealed radiation implant. Which precaution should the nurse implement?
A. Limit each visitor to 1 hour per day.
B. Keep dedicated equipment in the client’s room until the implant is removed.
C. Assign a different nurse to care for the client each day.
D. Place bed linens in a biohazard receptacle outside the client’s room.
Correct answer: C. Assign a different nurse to care for the client each day.
Topic: Oncology & Radiation
notes: Rationale:

Limit staff exposure by rotating nurses (time, distance, shielding). Visitors should be limited to about 30 minutes/day, and linens stay in the room until the implant is removed. Source note: dedicated equipment is listed as correct on other versions of this question, so check your instructor’s key.

slides.title: A fire with smoke is noted in the nurses’ station. Which action should the nurse
text: Question: A fire with smoke is noted in the nurses’ station. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Move clients close to a window with unit doors closed.
B. Use a bag valve mask to move a client on a mechanical ventilator.
C. Transfer clients by elevator to another floor.
D. Extinguish the fire starting at the ceiling and moving down.
Correct answer: B. Use a bag valve mask to move a client on a mechanical ventilator.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
RACE: Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Extinguish. Ventilator-dependent clients are evacuated while manually ventilated. Never use elevators in a fire, and extinguish by aiming at the BASE of the fire (PASS).

slides.title: Which action by the nurse is an example of PRIMARY prevention?
text: Question: Which action by the nurse is an example of PRIMARY prevention?
A. Teaching foot care to a client with diabetes.
B. Referring a client who recently lost a spouse to a support group.
C. Recommending helmets when riding bicycles or motorcycles.
D. Teaching monthly breast self-examination.
Correct answer: C. Recommending helmets when riding bicycles or motorcycles.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:
Primary = prevent disease/injury before it occurs (vaccines, helmets, healthy diet). Screening/BSE is secondary; foot care and support groups limit progression/complications (tertiary).

slides.title: The nurse is about to give scheduled immunizations to an immunocompromised child
text: Question: The nurse is about to give scheduled immunizations to an immunocompromised child. Which should the nurse question?
A. Haemophilus influenzae type B.
B. Inactivated poliovirus.
C. Hepatitis B.
D. Live attenuated influenza.
Correct answer: D. Live attenuated influenza.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Live vaccines (LAIV, MMR, varicella, rotavirus) are contraindicated in immunocompromised clients. Inactivated vaccines are safe.

slides.title: The nurse is teaching the mother of a 9-year-old child about age-appropriate toy
text: Question: The nurse is teaching the mother of a 9-year-old child about age-appropriate toys. Which is appropriate?
A. Finger paints and bubbles.
B. Board games and reading books.
C. Large building blocks and balls.
D. Wooden puzzles.
Correct answer: B. Board games and reading books.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
School-age (6–12) children are industrious: cooperative play, rules, board games, collections, reading, and sports. The other toys suit toddlers and preschoolers.

slides.title: At a health fair, for which client is it a priority to recommend follow-up with
text: Question: At a health fair, for which client is it a priority to recommend follow-up with a PHCP?
A. 65 y/o with elevated HDL, decreased LDL, and who does not follow a low-cholesterol diet.
B. 55 y/o with BP 164/96 mm Hg who stopped smoking 2 months ago.
C. 50 y/o with a family history of ovarian cancer who has not had the HPV vaccine.
D. 45 y/o with exercise-induced asthma and vesicular breath sounds in the peripheral lung fields.
Correct answer: B. 55 y/o with BP 164/96 mm Hg who stopped smoking 2 months ago.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
BP 164/96 is stage 2 hypertension and needs evaluation. High HDL and low LDL are desirable, and vesicular peripheral breath sounds are normal.

slides.title: In a well-baby clinic, it is most important to suggest follow-up for the infant
text: Question: In a well-baby clinic, it is most important to suggest follow-up for the infant who is
A. 6 months old and unable to roll over.
B. 4 months old and the posterior fontanel is closed.
C. 3 months old and unable to switch objects between hands.
D. 4 months old and sleeps up to 9 hours at night.
Correct answer: A. 6 months old and unable to roll over.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
By ~6 months infants roll both ways, so this is a gross-motor delay. The posterior fontanel closes at 2–3 months, hand-to-hand transfer comes around 6 months, and 9-hour sleep is normal.

slides.title: The parent of a child with leukemia is sitting at the bedside crying and says, “
text: Question: The parent of a child with leukemia is sitting at the bedside crying and says, “I’m so worried about my child.” Which response is most therapeutic?
A. “I’ll stay here and sit with you awhile.”
B. “Are you able to take good care of yourself?”
C. “Have you considered attending a support group?”
D. “Life must seem very scary right now.”
Correct answer: A. “I’ll stay here and sit with you awhile.”
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Offering presence is the most therapeutic response for a distressed parent. Other options are closed-ended, give advice prematurely, or put words in the parent’s mouth.

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comprehensive B" gives a different answer: "“Life must seem very scary right now.”". Yours here is "“I’ll stay here and sit with you awhile.”". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: The nurse is planning care for a client with histrionic personality disorder. Wh
text: Question: The nurse is planning care for a client with histrionic personality disorder. Which intervention is appropriate?
A. Work with the client on ways to develop trusting relationships.
B. Communicate with the client using concrete and descriptive language.
C. Have the client remain quiet and observe during group therapy.
D. Use compassionate behavior to keep the client in control.
Correct answer: B. Communicate with the client using concrete and descriptive language.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Cluster B/histrionic clients are dramatic and vague. Use concrete, direct, descriptive communication and set clear limits.

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comprehensive B" gives a different answer: "Work with the client on ways to develop trusting relationships.". Yours here is "Communicate with the client using concrete and descriptive language.". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: On a mental health unit, which client should the nurse assess first?
text: Question: On a mental health unit, which client should the nurse assess first?
A. Bipolar disorder, manic, no sleep in 24 hours, pacing the hallways.
B. Major depressive disorder overheard saying, “I can’t take it anymore.”
C. Suicidal ideation, reluctantly discussing a suicide contract with staff.
D. Anorexia nervosa who went to the restroom 15 minutes after a meal.
Correct answer: B. Major depressive disorder overheard saying, “I can’t take it anymore.”
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:

Safety first. A statement like “I can’t take it anymore” may signal suicidal intent, and no one has assessed it yet. Review sheet: assess the client with depression who says “I can’t do this anymore” first.

slides.title: A parent of a 3-year-old says the child is in constant motion and cannot sit thr
text: Question: A parent of a 3-year-old says the child is in constant motion and cannot sit through a story, and asks if the child is hyperactive. Which response is most appropriate?
A. “It is normal for parents to worry about hyperactivity.”
B. “I am not seeing any obvious signs of hyperactivity.”
C. “At 3 years of age, it is hard to tell.”
D. “Describe when and where this occurs.”
Correct answer: D. “Describe when and where this occurs.”
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Use therapeutic communication: open-ended exploration to gather data. Reassurance and dismissive responses block communication.

slides.title: The nurse is teaching the partner of a client who had a stroke. Which statement
text: Question: The nurse is teaching the partner of a client who had a stroke. Which statement indicates a need for additional teaching?
A. “I will make sure my partner has a snack 1 to 2 hours before going to bed.”
B. “I should have my partner alternate a bite of food with sips of water.”
C. “A change in my partner’s voice after swallowing may indicate dysphagia.”
D. “Hesitancy to eat could indicate difficulty swallowing.”
Correct answer: A. “I will make sure my partner has a snack 1 to 2 hours before going to bed.”
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Aspiration risk: with dysphagia, avoid eating close to bedtime and stay upright after meals. Wet or gurgly voice after swallowing and reluctance to eat are signs of dysphagia. (Key per source.)

slides.title: A client with GERD has been taught diet and lifestyle changes. Which statement i
text: Question: A client with GERD has been taught diet and lifestyle changes. Which statement indicates a need for additional teaching?
A. “I will sit upright for 1 to 2 hours after meals.”
B. “I will have a snack 1 hour before bedtime.”
C. “I will avoid tight clothing.”
D. “I will sleep with the head of my bed elevated 6 to 12 inches.”
Correct answer: B. “I will have a snack 1 hour before bedtime.”
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Do not eat within 2–3 hours of lying down. Eating before bed increases reflux. The other statements are correct.

slides.title: A newly hired nurse is caring for a client who died of pneumonia. Which action r
text: Question: A newly hired nurse is caring for a client who died of pneumonia. Which action requires intervention by the charge nurse?
A. Attaching 2 ID tags to the body and 1 on the outside of the shroud.
B. Leaving drainage tubes and IV lines in the body prior to autopsy.
C. Leaving any jewelry on the client to be transported to the funeral home.
D. Asking the family if they wish to participate in bathing the body.
Correct answer: C. Leaving any jewelry on the client to be transported to the funeral home.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:

Remove jewelry and give it to the family, documenting the transfer (a wedding band may be left only per policy). Tubes/lines are left in if an autopsy is expected, and family participation is encouraged.

slides.title: The client has a new order for graduated compression stockings. Which action sho
text: Question: The client has a new order for graduated compression stockings. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Measure the size of the client’s foot.
B. Apply the stockings while the client is sitting in a chair.
C. Check the stockings for wrinkles or creases.
D. Remove the stockings once each day for 10 minutes.
Correct answer: C. Check the stockings for wrinkles or creases.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:

Wrinkles act like a tourniquet and impair circulation. Measure the LEG, apply before rising (supine, legs elevated), and remove for ~30 minutes at least every 8–24 hours per policy for skin care and assessment.

slides.title: The nurse is preparing a Mantoux test. Which action indicates correct technique?
text: Question: The nurse is preparing a Mantoux test. Which action indicates correct technique?
A. Injecting in the subcutaneous tissue.
B. Drawing up 0.1 mL of PPD tuberculin.
C. Using a 20-gauge needle.
D. Inserting the needle at a 90-degree angle.
Correct answer: B. Drawing up 0.1 mL of PPD tuberculin.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Mantoux = intradermal injection of 0.1 mL PPD with a 25–27 gauge, ⅜–½ inch needle at 5–15° (bevel up) to raise a wheal.

slides.title: A client is receiving O positive packed red blood cells. The client’s blood type
text: Question: A client is receiving O positive packed red blood cells. The client’s blood type is B positive. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Administer acetaminophen and diphenhydramine PRN.
B. Immediately stop the transfusion.
C. Document on an incident report.
D. Continue to assess the client.
Correct answer: D. Continue to assess the client.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
O-negative is the universal donor, and O blood is ABO-compatible with a B-positive recipient. The Rh factor matches, so the transfusion is compatible. Continue to monitor for reactions.

slides.title: A PHCP prescribes vaccines for an older adult. Which should the nurse clarify?
text: Question: A PHCP prescribes vaccines for an older adult. Which should the nurse clarify?
A. Inactivated polio (IPV) series.
B. Influenza (quadrivalent).
C. Herpes zoster (Zostavax).
D. Tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis (Tdap) booster.
Correct answer: A. Inactivated polio (IPV) series.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:

Older adults routinely receive influenza, pneumococcal, Td/Tdap and zoster. Polio vaccine is not routinely given to adults unless at risk or unvaccinated, so clarify it. (Zostavax was a live vaccine that has since been replaced by the recombinant Shingrix.)

slides.title: A client is prescribed warfarin for a prosthetic heart valve. Which finding indi
text: Question: A client is prescribed warfarin for a prosthetic heart valve. Which finding indicates a therapeutic effect?
A. PT of 11.6 seconds.
B. PTT of 20 seconds.
C. aPTT of 35 seconds.
D. INR of 3.
Correct answer: D. INR of 3.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Therapeutic INR on warfarin is 2–3 (2.5–3.5 for mechanical valves). A PT of 11.6 s is normal (not anticoagulated); PTT/aPTT monitor heparin.

slides.title: The nurse starts LR for a burn client prescribed 5,200 mL over the first 24 hour
text: Question: The nurse starts LR for a burn client prescribed 5,200 mL over the first 24 hours (half in the first 8 hours). How many mL/hr for the first 8 hours?
A. 350 mL/hr
B. 433 mL/hr
C. 325 mL/hr
D. 217 mL/hr
Correct answer: C. 325 mL/hr
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
Half of 5,200 = 2,600 mL in 8 hours → 2,600 ÷ 8 = 325 mL/hr.

slides.title: Which action is appropriate when preparing to administer insulin to an adult?
text: Question: Which action is appropriate when preparing to administer insulin to an adult?
A. Limit the dose to 1 mL when injecting into the deltoid muscle.
B. Insert the needle at a 15-degree angle.
C. Draw up the dose using a 25-gauge, ⅜-inch needle.
D. Administer the dose using the Z-track method.
Correct answer: C. Draw up the dose using a 25-gauge, ⅜-inch needle.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Insulin is subcutaneous: 25–30 gauge, ⅜–⅝ inch needle at 45–90°. Z-track and deltoid volume limits are IM techniques; 15° is intradermal.

slides.title: A client is receiving streptomycin. Which finding indicates an adverse effect?
text: Question: A client is receiving streptomycin. Which finding indicates an adverse effect?
A. Increased liver enzymes.
B. Staining of the teeth.
C. Creatinine of 2.2 mg/dL.
D. Photosensitivity.
Correct answer: C. Creatinine of 2.2 mg/dL.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Aminoglycosides (“-mycin”) are nephrotoxic and ototoxic. Elevated creatinine shows kidney injury. Teeth staining/photosensitivity are tetracycline effects.

slides.title: A client who had a spontaneous abortion is taught about Rho(D) immune globulin.
text: Question: A client who had a spontaneous abortion is taught about Rho(D) immune globulin. Which statement indicates a need for further teaching?
A. “This medication will allow for safe mixing of my blood with the baby’s in future pregnancies.”
B. “The medication could cause redness or mild pain at the injection site.”
C. “This medication will prevent potential loss of pregnancy in the future.”
D. “The medication will help my body fully remove the placenta lining.”
Correct answer: D. “The medication will help my body fully remove the placenta lining.”
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
RhoGAM prevents an Rh-negative mother from forming antibodies against Rh-positive fetal cells. It has no effect on removing the placenta or uterine lining. Injection-site soreness is expected.

slides.title: A client with a history of PUD in the ED has BP 110/72, P 90, yellow emesis, fre
text: Question: A client with a history of PUD in the ED has BP 110/72, P 90, yellow emesis, frequent belching, Hgb 9.2 g/dL. What is the priority?
A. Determine if the client has any stressors.
B. Type and cross for a PRBC transfusion.
C. Administer an IV antiemetic.
D. Prepare the client for surgery.
Correct answer: C. Administer an IV antiemetic.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:

Stable vital signs with no signs of active hemorrhage mean the immediate problem is vomiting. Controlling it prevents aspiration, dehydration and electrolyte loss. Compare: with hypotension (e.g., 92/58) bleeding is suspected and the priority changes.

slides.title: During labor with fetal monitoring, the FHR has been 180 for 12 minutes. What sh
text: Question: During labor with fetal monitoring, the FHR has been 180 for 12 minutes. What should the nurse do first?
A. Assist the client with guided imagery.
B. Continue to monitor the FHR.
C. Turn the client to their left side.
D. Prepare the client for cesarean delivery.
Correct answer: C. Turn the client to their left side.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:

FHR >160 for 10 minutes is fetal tachycardia (possible hypoxia). First, use the least invasive intervention: left lateral position to relieve cord compression and improve placental perfusion, then give oxygen, IV fluids, and notify the provider.

slides.title: It is a priority to notify the PHCP if a client who
text: Question: It is a priority to notify the PHCP if a client who
A. has community-acquired pneumonia has WBC 15,000/mm³.
B. takes warfarin has an INR of 2.
C. has end-stage renal disease and a creatinine of 2.7 mg/dL.
D. has heart failure and a sodium of 125 mEq/L.
Correct answer: D. has heart failure and a sodium of 125 mEq/L.
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Sodium 125 is critically low (normal 135–145) and risks seizures and confusion. Elevated WBC in pneumonia, INR 2 on warfarin, and elevated creatinine in ESRD are all expected.

slides.title: A client 4 hours post-op after general anesthesia has T 98.4° F, P 58, BP 98/64,
text: Question: A client 4 hours post-op after general anesthesia has T 98.4° F, P 58, BP 98/64, shallow respirations at 26, pale dry skin; ABG pH 7.20, PaCO₂ 54, HCO₃ 26. Which findings relate to the ABG? 1 IV fluids; 2 BP; 3 pulse; 4 temperature; 5 urine output; 6 general anesthesia; 7 pale dry skin; 8 shallow respirations.
Correct answer: A. 2, 3, 6, 7, 8
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
This is acute respiratory acidosis (low pH, high CO₂, normal HCO₃). Anesthesia depresses respiration → shallow breathing → CO₂ retention, with hypotension, bradycardia, and pale skin.

slides.title: In a pediatric cardiac unit, which child should the nurse assess first?
text: Question: In a pediatric cardiac unit, which child should the nurse assess first?
A. 2-year-old walking in the playroom with a pulse of 150.
B. 6-year-old sitting and eating a snack with a pulse of 130.
C. 16-year-old sleeping with a pulse of 55.
D. 2-month-old crying with a pulse of 170.
Correct answer: B. 6-year-old sitting and eating a snack with a pulse of 130.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Know pediatric norms. A resting 6-year-old should be ~75–120 bpm, so 130 is abnormal. The others are acceptable for activity/crying/sleeping.

slides.title: A client with lung cancer is receiving external radiation therapy. Which stateme
text: Question: A client with lung cancer is receiving external radiation therapy. Which statement shows understanding?
A. “I will need to avoid eating raw fruits and vegetables.”
B. “I should avoid close contact with anyone who is pregnant or children under 12.”
C. “I will need to avoid direct skin exposure to the sun during treatment and for at least 1 year afterward.”
D. “I should apply 50-SPF sunscreen to the radiation area before going out.”
Correct answer: C. “I will need to avoid direct skin exposure to the sun during treatment and for at least 1 year afterward.”
Topic: Oncology & Radiation
notes: Rationale:
Irradiated skin stays sensitive for a year or more, so protect it from sun. External radiation does not make the client radioactive. Don’t apply products to the site unless prescribed.

slides.title: A client had a kidney transplant 1 week ago. It is a priority to notify the PHCP
text: Question: A client had a kidney transplant 1 week ago. It is a priority to notify the PHCP if the client has
A. fluid intake of 1,000 mL and urine output of 800 mL over 8 hours.
B. a temperature rise from 98.2 to 99.3° F over 4 hours.
C. a WBC decrease from 6,000 to 5,000/mm³.
D. a weight increase from 199 to 203 lb over 24 hours.
Correct answer: D. a weight increase from 199 to 203 lb over 24 hours.
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
A gain of 4 lb in 24 hours (about 2 L of fluid) signals fluid retention and possible acute rejection. The other values are minor.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client who develops the following rhythm (premature wi
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client who develops the following rhythm (premature wide, bizarre QRS complexes with inverted T waves — PVCs). Which action should the nurse take?
A. Determine if the client has an internal pacemaker.
B. Check the client’s potassium level.
C. Place a defibrillator at the bedside.
D. Notify the rapid response team.
Correct answer: B. Check the client’s potassium level.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:

Isolated PVCs are commonly caused by electrolyte imbalance (especially low K⁺ or Mg²⁺), hypoxia, or ischemia. Check the potassium level and notify the provider if it is abnormal. (Rhythm strip was an image in your PDF.)

slides.title: A client had gastric surgery 8 hours ago and has an NG tube to low suction. Whic
text: Question: A client had gastric surgery 8 hours ago and has an NG tube to low suction. Which interventions belong in the plan? 1 Turn down the suction when assessing for peristalsis. 2 Encourage IS every 4 hours while awake. 3 Maintain SCDs. 4 Irrigate the NG with warm tap water as needed. 5 Turn and reposition every 2 hours. 6 Place a sign: “Do not manipulate the NG tube.”
Correct answer: B. 3, 5, 6
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:

After gastric surgery, the NG tube must not be moved or irrigated without a surgeon’s order (protect the suture line). SCDs and q2h turning prevent VTE and pressure injury. Suction should be turned OFF to auscultate. IS is needed every 1–2 hours, and irrigation uses sterile normal saline, never tap water.

slides.title: After tracheostomy care, which finding requires intervention before leaving the
text: Question: After tracheostomy care, which finding requires intervention before leaving the room?
A. The client places a finger over the tube opening when speaking.
B. The cuff can be easily inflated and deflated.
C. There is space for 1 finger between the tie and the neck.
D. The tube moves in and out of the stoma when the client coughs.
Correct answer: D. The tube moves in and out of the stoma when the client coughs.
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
Tube movement means the ties are too loose and the tube can dislodge or be expelled. Fix it. A one-finger gap is correct; occluding the opening to speak is expected (speaking valve/finger).

slides.title: A client on mechanical ventilation has a low-pressure alarm. Which action should
text: Question: A client on mechanical ventilation has a low-pressure alarm. Which action should the nurse take next?
A. Shut the alarm off and call a code.
B. Assess the cuff of the client’s endotracheal tube.
C. Manually ventilate with a bag-mask-valve device.
D. Call respiratory therapy to check the ventilator settings.
Correct answer: B. Assess the cuff of the client’s endotracheal tube.
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
Low-pressure alarm = a leak: disconnected tubing, cuff leak, or flat pilot balloon. Assess the client and the cuff. Never silence the alarm without finding the cause.

slides.title: The nurse provides discharge teaching to parents of a child admitted with sickle
text: Question: The nurse provides discharge teaching to parents of a child admitted with sickle cell crisis. Which instruction should be included?
A. “Monitor your child’s temperature daily.”
B. “Restrict play activity to 1 hour per day.”
C. “Avoid areas with low altitude.”
D. “Maintain a warm temperature in your home.”
Correct answer: D. “Maintain a warm temperature in your home.”
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Cold causes vasoconstriction and sickling, so keep the home warm and avoid cold exposure, dehydration, and HIGH altitude (low oxygen). Also report fever promptly. Don’t restrict normal activity.

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comprehensive B" gives a different answer: "“Monitor your child’s temperature daily.”". Yours here is "“Maintain a warm temperature in your home.”". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: An older adult with dementia often tells stories to cope with anxiety. The nurse
text: Question: An older adult with dementia often tells stories to cope with anxiety. The nurse recognizes confabulation when the client
A. tells made-up stories.
B. refuses to see family members.
C. displays ritualistic behaviors.
D. reminisces about the past.
Correct answer: A. tells made-up stories.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Confabulation = unconsciously filling memory gaps with fabricated stories. Refusing family is withdrawal, rituals are compulsions, and reminiscing is normal life review.
